item.title: ‘Frog toxin’ that killed Navalny was likely lab-made, says expert
item.description: The 'frog' poison that killed Navalny was hard to hide and likely made in a high-end lab, according to a Belgian toxicologist.

item.title: Right of Reply: FIDE responds to ‘EU travel ban could see Russia’s world chess head challenged for top role’
item.description: The Swiss-based International Chess Federation or World Chess Federation (FIDE) rejects allegations that its president, Arkady Dvorkovich, backed Russia’s invasion or organised events in occupied Ukraine, arguing claims misrepresent his honorary CFR role and federation decisions.

item.title: EU promises new aid to address Africa’s Great Lakes refugee crisis
item.description: The EU's crisis commissioner Hadja Lahbib has made a three-day visit to eastern DR Congo and Burundi this week, to see for herself the scale of the refugee crisis.

item.title: How Orbán systematically suffocated the Hungarian media over the past 15 years
item.description: Viktor Orbán has also pledged, in his annual address earlier this month, to “clear out” after the April elections media and civil society organisations deemed to threaten “sovereignty.” Fidesz already directly or indirectly control 80 percent of Hungary's media.

item.title: Listen: Has the EU given up on participating in the peace negotiations between Ukraine and Russia?
item.description: The peace talks between Ukraine and Russia started in Abu Dhabi last month and continued in Geneva this week, but do not include the EU. Apart from being informed, how is the EU contributing to peace efforts?

item.title: EU racing to agree more Russia sanctions for Ukraine-invasion anniversary
item.description: Hungary and Slovakia risk delaying new EU sanctions on Russia, but Malta is falling into line, less than a week before Europe's Ukraine-anniversary deadline.

item.title: ‘We are a player, not just a payer’: EU Commission defends attendance at Trump’s Peace Board
item.description: The European Commission says their presence at Donald Trump's Board of Peace is needed because they have invested heavily in Gaza - despite reported objections from France and Spain.

item.title: 52 days to election: Orbán escalates Ukraine row, AI execution video shocks Hungary’s election campaign
item.description: In this week's digest from the Hungarian election campaign trail: Ukraine oil rows, Viktor Orban vows to finish off the job against civil society and independent media after April election and accuses the Shell oil company of being behind the opposition.

item.title: Top European AI boss warns of US tech concentration at India summit
item.description: The CEO of Paris-based Mistral, often touted as a European AI champion, raised concerns over the concentration of AI power in a few companies during the global summit in India, while political leaders focused on tech safety.

item.title: Poland’s Sikorski says the quiet bit out loud: Europe has become Ukraine’s lifeline, not US
item.description: Last year, Europe became Ukraine’s main supporter, providing over $200bn (€170bn) in military, financial, and humanitarian aid, while US assistance dropped sharply, shifting the war’s centre of gravity to the EU.
